column4: Seth Moran (written communication) "Noticed an elevated signal at VALT that lasted several hours, we're having a major rain event right now, and the signal also shows up faintly at SUG, and not other stations, probably a debris flow down one of the channels draining the glacier"

Heavy rain on October 22 (about 5 inches on the south side of MSH, somewhat less to the north) coincided with seismic and AFM signals indicating possible debris flows. Rainfall total and intensity appear to be less than seen about one year earlier, during the September 28-30, 2013 rain event. AFM signals were also smaller than seen during the 2013 event. To document, I hiked out to upper SF Toutle on 10-23 and observed elevated muddy stream flow, but in the channel directly adjacent to the AFM, and to downstream, did not see deposits indicative of debris flow, just reworked channel. However, about 650 meters upstream, at the limit of my view, there does appear to be a debris flow deposit (see photos 150, 159, and 160). I believe the debris flow stopped in this area, but would have resulted in a lot of material moving down through the AFM reach, just not as a coherent
debris flow. On Nov. 1, inspection of the NF Toutle from the Hummocks Trail area to the confluence of Loowit and Step creeks also showed elevated muddy flow and braided, shallow channels. Again, I did not see much evidence of a coherent debris flow (one or two questionable deposits)--just mostly worked over river channel, with a significant
amount of bank erosion. I did not get upstream enough to verify if a small debris flow or flows might have come out of the crater, but based on AFM signals, I'd say probably not. Might be able to verify this on next visit to Loowit AFM. For a view of the channel below the Loowit/Step confluence, see the attached video.
